Spec / why: FREE, open source. gr-iridium takes raw IQ, runs an FFT burst detector, downmixes each burst, does carrier and timing recovery, demodulates QPSK and emits bit frames; iridium-toolkit decodes them. THE POINT FOR THIS PROJECT: it reports PER-BURST FREQUENCY, so the Doppler shift is directly measurable on the ground. That replaces the 180m sigma / 2s latency model in sitl/soop_link.py with MEASURED numbers. The sigma was [A] 20m until 2026-09-04; it is now [L] 180m, the published Iridium NEXT figure without elevation aiding. 20m turned out to be the best result in the literature - four Iridium plus one Orbcomm, five satellites across two constellations, static receiver - being applied to single-constellation Iridium on a moving quad. NOTE the dominant error is EPHEMERIS, not the receiver: TLE orbit error is kilometres and is the main source of positioning inaccuracy, so no better SDR, TCXO, LNA or antenna raises the accuracy ceiling. They raise SNR, which you need to detect bursts at all.
Provenance: [D] muccc/gr-iridium README: FFT burst detect, QPSK demod, frame output

Spec / why: Nose camera recording to its own microSD. Chosen over a RunCam-class action cam because it does the same job for a fifth of the price. OV2640/OV3660 + microSD + 8MB PSRAM; with the open-source ESP32-CAM_MJPEG2SD firmware it writes ~20 fps AVI to the card (a naive JPEG-per-frame loop gets ~1 fps at SVGA - use the firmware). WIFI AND ESP-NOW MUST STAY OFF IN FLIGHT - the RC link is 2.4GHz ELRS and an ESP32 radiating 2.4GHz centimetres from the receiver can desensitise it, which is a control-link failure, not a video glitch. ESP-NOW cannot carry video anyway (~250 byte payloads). For LIVE video later, that is a 5.8GHz analogue AIO cam+VTX off the VBAT pad PF1 plus a UVC receiver the laptop sees as a webcam - separate purchase. Rolling shutter on a quad means jello: soft-mount it. IT CANNOT ALSO BE THE OPTICAL FLOW SENSOR, and not for one reason but four: one camera cannot face both down (flow) and forward (recording); its OV2640/OV3660 is ROLLING shutter, which prop vibration turns into jello that corrupts flow - the deferred flow camera is an OV9281 GLOBAL shutter part for exactly this reason; the sensor emits JPEG or raw, not both, and recording needs the in-sensor JPEG to stay inside the CPU budget; and SD writes stall 100ms+ during wear-levelling, which a recorder absorbs but a position-estimate loop cannot. Use a PMW3901-based module for flow - it computes flow in-sensor and needs no camera pipeline. See docs/SENSORS.md.

Item: Servo BEC (only if a servo is ever fitted)
Spec / why: VSERVO (J10 pin 3, and the TP22 pad) is DELIBERATELY NOT connected to the board's +5V rail: that rail has about 0.65 A of headroom and one stalled hobby servo exceeds it, which would brown out the flight controller in flight. So a servo's power comes from its own BEC, wired to TP22. Nothing on this build uses a servo - J10 is payload provisioning - so this is LATER, not TO BUY. Listed because 'the servo port needs an external BEC' was written in the design and in no buying document, which is exactly how a missing part reaches the bench.

Item: Bench power supply, adjustable with CURRENT LIMIT
Spec / why: REQUIRED BY T1 AND NOT SUBSTITUTABLE BY THE SMOKE STOPPER. docs/BUILD.md T1 says 'Bench supply on VBAT, current limit 100 mA, 16.8 V' with USB disconnected, and the whole point is that a rail fault draws its limit instead of destroying the MCU - expected draw is under 80 mA, so anything over that means stop. A smoke stopper limits INRUSH from a battery; it cannot hold a 100 mA ceiling or show you the number. Needs 0-20 V at 1 A minimum, which is the cheapest class of bench PSU there is. SKIP THIS ROW IF YOU ALREADY OWN ONE - it is listed because 'soldering iron and basic tools' does not cover it and T1 is the step that protects a GBP 190 board.

Spec / why: REQUIRED BY T3a, which docs/BUILD.md calls 'not optional'. U9's peak junction models at 179 C on the AP2112 datasheet's no-heatsink figure against a 150 C limit, and 116 C on good copper; U8 reaches 139 C on JEDEC copper against 125 C. Both are BRACKETS, not computed values - this board sits between the two and only a measurement says where. It is the one modelled number left that can still be wrong in the bad direction, and being wrong means a mid-flight brownout rather than smoke, because the AP2112 has thermal shutdown. A K-type thermocouple meter is better than IR on parts this small (a SOT-23-5 is smaller than most IR spot sizes); either is acceptable per BUILD.md line 616.
